item.title: Software Protection and Licensing Landscape: From Keygens to Denuvo, Why Local Verification Always Breaks
item.description: In February 2026, a tool called Hypervisor appeared that could bypass Denuvo anti-tamper without a game-specific crack — the price being that Secure Boot and a few Windows virtualization features had to be turned off. By April, the community confirmed that every single-player, non-VR game previously protected by Denuvo was vulnerable to the method. In September, the group RUNE stripped Denuvo out of Assassin’s Creed Mirage entirely; Denuvo responded by shipping updated protection versions and filing a DMCA lawsuit against the distributors. Four decades into the software licensing arms race that began with serial numbers, the strongest commercial anti-tamper scheme now holds out for a matter of months.
